item: Row 382 (R800): the custody chain verify says whether this installation's custody key signed the chain
summary: GET /api/custody/{item}/verify checked each entry against the key it carries and anchored the lineage on the last entry's own key, so a verified chain said nothing about who signed it. A verified reply now carries signed_by and signer_key for THE ITEM asked about, decided by the rule POST /verify uses for a whole-log bundle (log.item_signer: each of the item's entries is this installation's only where _own_positions places one of its identities, both halves, an earlier key only through endorsed rotations, and _is_yours holds), against this installation's custody identity read as POST /verify reads it (no key or folder created); a custody key with an R801 marker beside it (asked through evidence.is_this_installations_key) is never this installation's. States: this-installation (every item entry), another-installation (none, and none carries this installation's Ed25519 key), not-compared (mixed, an uncredited entry under this installation's key such as one stripped of its post-quantum half, or no readable key); signer_key is the item's last entry's Ed25519 key; a chain that does not verify names no signer. The log is read once (verify_report takes the entries), so the answer is about the entries verified. The two security reads' must-fixes (whole-log last entry instead of the item; the ML-DSA half not compared; a second read) are folded in. The custody view shows R800's existing labels x12; no new strings; what a chain is accepted as is unchanged. Known gap, ruled as row 393 (R816): a restore places custody and annotations keys with no R801 marker, so until that lands a custody key restored from another computer reads as this installation's here and in POST /verify.
